context: You have a part-time job at the city's public transit information center. Listen to the customer service supervisor and repeat what he says.
visual: A busy counter in a train station with a large route map on the wall and screens showing departure times.
sentences: Most questions are about delays.
Weekly passes are sold at window three.
Trains to the airport leave every fifteen minutes until midnight.
Passengers who lose a ticket must fill out a form before receiving a replacement.
The route map shows all twelve lines, which are marked with different colors and numbers.
Students who show a valid university card can buy a monthly pass for forty-five pounds instead of sixty.
If passengers ask about the night buses, explain that they run only on Fridays and Saturdays, from one until five.

context: You are volunteering at the information desk of a university hospital. Listen to the volunteer coordinator and repeat what she says.
visual: A hospital lobby with a reception desk, a row of elevators and colored lines on the floor leading to different departments.
sentences: Visiting hours begin at noon.
Always wear your badge where patients can see it.
The colored lines on the floor lead visitors to each department.
The children's ward, which is on the fourth floor, has its own separate entrance.
Never give out information about a patient's condition, even to people who say they are close family members.
Visitors who arrive after eight in the evening must sign in with the security guard at the main door.
When the lobby gets crowded, which usually happens around two o'clock, guide visitors toward the stairs instead of the elevators.

context: You are training as a guide at a railway museum located in a historic train station. Listen to the museum curator and repeat what he says.
visual: A large hall with a glass roof, an old green steam locomotive and wooden benches from the original station.
sentences: This station opened in eighteen eighty-two.
The glass roof was restored after the war.
Over two hundred trains a day once stopped at these platforms.
The steam locomotive in the center of the hall weighs nearly ninety tons.
These wooden benches, which were made by local carpenters, are the only original furniture that survived.
During the nineteen thirties, the station employed about six hundred workers, many of whom lived in the streets nearby.
Children may climb into the driver's cabin of the locomotive, but only when a trained member of staff is beside them.

context: You have started working in the special collections room of the university library, where rare books and old documents are kept. Listen to the archivist and repeat what she says.
visual: A quiet reading room with long tables, foam book supports, white cotton gloves and shelves of old leather-bound books behind glass.
sentences: Pens are not allowed in this room.
Readers must use pencils to take notes.
Each book must be placed on a foam support while it is open.
Our oldest manuscript, which dates from the twelfth century, is kept in a separate vault.
Readers can request up to five items at a time, but they must return each one before leaving.
The temperature in this room is kept at eighteen degrees, which protects the paper from damage caused by heat and humidity.
If readers want to photograph a document published less than seventy years ago, they need written permission from the copyright holder.

context: You are helping to organize a regional high school science fair hosted by your university. Listen to the head judge and repeat what he says.
visual: A gymnasium filled with rows of tables and colorful poster boards, with students standing beside their projects.
sentences: Judging starts at ten o'clock.
Each judge will receive a scoring sheet.
There are one hundred and twenty projects in this year's competition.
Every project must be evaluated by at least three judges working independently.
Students whose projects involve live animals need to show a signed approval form from their teacher.
The judges will spend about eight minutes at each table, which includes time for the student to answer questions.
The three projects that receive the highest average scores will be invited to the national competition, which takes place next spring.

context: You have a summer job at the visitor center of a coastal wind farm. Listen to the site engineer and repeat what she says.
visual: A row of tall white wind turbines along a cliff above the sea, with a small visitor center and a viewing platform in front.
sentences: Visitors must stay behind the fence.
Each turbine is one hundred meters tall.
The blades turn more slowly than most people expect.
Together, the thirty turbines produce enough electricity for about forty thousand homes.
The turbines stop automatically when the wind speed reaches ninety kilometers per hour, which protects the blades.
The viewing platform, which was built last spring, offers the best view of the turbines that stand closest to the sea.
Guests who want to see inside a turbine can join the guided tour that leaves the visitor center at eleven and three.
